To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
immunohistochemical staining and mutational status are not associated with disease‐free survival in patients with GISTs who have undergone curative resection without adjuvant therapy.
immunohistochemical staining for KIT and PDGFR‐α is not associated with disease‐free survival in GIST patients after resection of their primary tumor without ad juvant therapy.
immunohistochemical PDGFRA expression and PDGFRA mutation in GISTs were not associated with prognosis, whereas KIT immunohistochemical staining was a significant prognostic marker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of new diagnostic tools for the detection of the most common mutations in the KIT and PDGFR‐A genes.
the development of a new generation of high performance computing systems and algorithms for the numerical solution of partial differential equations.

the following: 1. the role of the KIT/PDGFRA pathway in the pathogenesis and progression of gastrointestinal stromal tumors; 2. the role of KIT/PDGRRA pathway in the prognosis of patients with primary gastrointestinal stromal tumor; 3. the role of PDGFA in the pathogenesis of primary gastrointestinal stromals tumors; and 4. the role of immunohistochemical PDGFRA in the prognosis of gastrointestinal stromal tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutational status of the GISTs does not seem to influence the outcome of patients who have undergone surgery.
immunohistochemical PDGFRA expression is a prognostic marker for GISTs, whereas the prognostic significance of KIT and the mutational status of both KIT and PDGFR‐α remains unclear.

there is no evidence that the immunohistochemical staining of KIT and the mutational status of PDGFRA and KIT are of any value for prognosis after curative surgery for gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KIT and PDGFRα immunohistochemistry are not associated with the risk of relapse in GISTs.
the expression of PDGF‐RA in GIST is not associated with the clinical and pathological features, and the mutational status of the KIT gene is not associated with prognosis.

the mutational status of GISTs does not seem to be associated with the clinical behavior and prognosis of GISTs, and that the expression of KIT and/or PDGFRA is a more reliable prognostic marker for GISTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunohistochemical analysis of KIT and/or PDGFRA is a useful tool to identify patients at risk for relapse after curative resected GIST.
the mutational status of GISTs is not predictive of clinical outcome.
the mutational status of PDGFRA and the expression of PDGF‐alpha in GISTs may predict the risk of recurrence in GIST patients after curative resections of the primary tumor.
